body:
In version 0.28.0, query params are never merged.

```python
import httpx

client = httpx.Client()
request = client.build_request(
    "GET", "https://httpbin.org/get?param=default", params={"foo": "bar"}
)
print(request.url)  # This will be `https://httpbin.org/get?foo=bar`
```

The query string in the request url will be ignored. It seems this is caused by the pr #3364. Params are replaced instead of merged when parsing. https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/15e21e9ea3cad4f06e22a7e704aabefdf43d2e29/httpx/_urlparse.py#L301

Related discussion https://github.com/encode/httpx/discussions/3428

comments.author: yanyongyu
comments.body:
I know providing both params and query in url is a bad practice. But this can be counterintuitive in some situations like:

```python
import httpx

client = httpx.Client(params={"foo": "bar"})
request = client.build_request(
    "GET", "https://httpbin.org/get?param=default"
)
print(request.url)  # This will be `https://httpbin.org/get?foo=bar`
```

The params are provided in the client options. This will also replace the query in the url.

May be a warning can be raised when the replaced query is not empty?

https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/15e21e9ea3cad4f06e22a7e704aabefdf43d2e29/httpx/_urlparse.py#L301

comments.body: Currently, as a workaround, we merge all the params by ourselves before passing to httpx. The code is clearer logically :joy: .
